segments.text: > Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. `ReadableStream`, `WritableStream`, and `TransformStream` are the WHATWG (browser-standard) backbone of pipeline-style data processing. Node has its own, older, differently-shaped `stream` module — see the Node rows below — that real Node code (including `fs`/`http`/`child_process` internally) actually uses far more than the WHATWG API.

Full design: [TDD-00097](../tdd/TDD-00097.md) ([ADR-00296](../adr/ADR-00296.md)–[ADR-00302](../adr/ADR-00302.md), [ADR-00304](../adr/ADR-00304.md)). `pipeTo` (all four shutdown-propagation rules + `prevent*` + `AbortSignal`), `pipeThrough`, and `tee()` come with the rows below; in-memory pipelines run on the promise/microtask runtime alone — no fibers or libcurl. HTTP integration is tracked where it surfaces: fetch `Response.body` on [NETWORKING.md](NETWORKING.md), streaming response/request bodies on [HTTP-SERVER.md](HTTP-SERVER.md).

caveats: No BYOB readers / byte controllers (`type: 'bytes'` rejected at compile time)
`ReadableStream.from()` accepts arrays only, not async iterables
Source callbacks must be arrow/function-expression/method-shorthand literals; a cancel callback can't take a reason parameter

`read()` on a closed stream whose chunk type is an **array/tuple** (`ReadableStream<number[]>`) yields the chunk's zero-shaped value, not `undefined` (an array slot has no spare absent state — [ADR-00246](../adr/ADR-00246.md))
`releaseLock()` leaves queued pending reads pending instead of rejecting them
`values()` returns a reader usable in `for await` only (no standalone `.next()`)
In the no-fiber tier, `await` of an already-settled `read()` skips the microtask drain, so a pending pull can run one tick later than real JS
A synchronously-throwing pull/start propagates to the caller instead of erroring the stream
`tee()` forwards the last cancelling branch's reason instead of composing both; a signal abort of `pipeTo` takes effect at the next chunk boundary
notes: One 144-byte heap struct fuses stream + controller + reader (compile-time retyping); chunk queue + pending-read promise FIFO with HWM/size accounting; spec CallPullIfNeeded; per-site fulfill thunk builds typed `{value,done}` records ([ADR-00296](../adr/ADR-00296.md))
Runs on the promise/microtask runtime alone — no fibers or libcurl for in-memory pipelines
A scalar/string/object chunk reads a real `undefined`, and `controller.desiredSize` is `null` once errored ([TDD-00196](../tdd/TDD-00196.md), [ADR-00826](../adr/ADR-00826.md))

caveats: `releaseLock()` doesn't reject a pending-write view
A synchronously-throwing sink write propagates instead of erroring the stream (an async rejection is handled per spec)
A sink abort callback can't take a reason parameter; no transformer/sink `start` promise-vs-write interlock beyond the started flag
notes: 128-byte fused stream+controller+writer struct; 32-byte write-queue entries carry their own per-write promise; `ready` re-armed on backpressure flips ([ADR-00297](../adr/ADR-00297.md))

caveats: No transformer `start` callback
Cancelling the readable side doesn't error the writable side
An identity transform (no callback) requires matching I/O chunk representations
notes: Writable sink write runs the transform when the readable side has capacity, else parks the chunk (at most one, by write serialization); readable pull resumes it; spec defaults writable HWM 1 / readable HWM 0 ([ADR-00298](../adr/ADR-00298.md))

caveats: The format argument must be a string literal ("gzip", "deflate", "deflate-raw") — a runtime-computed format string is a compile error
Chunks are `Uint8Array` only (no ArrayBuffer/DataView BufferSource variants)
notes: A `%kml.ts` TransformStream context with native zlib transform/flush closures; `-lz` linked only when constructed; inflate auto-detects gzip/zlib wrappers ([ADR-00302](../adr/ADR-00302.md))

caveats: Delivers the blob's bytes as a **single** `Uint8Array` chunk (the whole blob), not incrementally chunked as a real byte source would be
notes: Returns a `ReadableStream<Uint8Array>` — one owned-copy chunk then closed; an empty blob yields no chunk ([ADR-00341](../adr/ADR-00341.md)). Consumable via `for await` or `.getReader()`

caveats: An omitted error argument reaches a callback declared `(err?: Error | null)` as `null`; Node passes `undefined` (the `write`/`end` callbacks, `finished`, `pipeline`)
`Readable.from` takes an array, a string or a Buffer; a generator or other iterable is not supported
The HTTP server's `req`/`res` are separate runtime handles, not instances of these classes: `instanceof Readable`, a subclass's methods and piping into one of these classes do not apply to them
`Readable.toWeb` enqueues each chunk as it arrives, without the web stream's pull backpressure; `Duplex.toWeb`/`Duplex.fromWeb` are missing

Not ported: `compose`, `addAbortSignal`, the readable operators (`map`/`filter`/`toArray`/…), `Readable.wrap`, `Duplex.from`, `stream.isReadable`/`isErrored`/`setDefaultHighWaterMark`, and the `signal` option
A method replaced on an instance (`this._read = fn`) is not supported; pass it in the options
notes: Node v24's `lib/internal/streams` ported to TypeScript (`lib/node/stream.ts`) and compiled with the program: the same states, event order and `process.nextTick` deferrals, the options form with `this`, class overrides, `setEncoding` via a `string_decoder`-like decoder, object mode, `highWaterMark` defaults (64 KiB, 16 objects), `destroy`/`autoDestroy`, `for await` ([ADR-01161](../adr/ADR-01161.md))

caveats: Function stages (`pipeline(src, async function* …)`) and the `signal` option are not supported — every stage is a stream
notes: Node's `pipelineImpl`/`destroyer` and end-of-stream (`willEmitClose`): the callback runs once the last stream has finished, or with the first error, every stream then destroyed; `finished` returns its cleanup function ([ADR-01161](../adr/ADR-01161.md))
`import { pipeline, finished } from 'stream/promises'`, over the callback forms ([ADR-01161](../adr/ADR-01161.md))
Two `Duplex` instances cross-wired as Node's `DuplexSide`: a write completes when the peer reads it, and `end()` finishes once the peer has ended ([ADR-01161](../adr/ADR-01161.md))
